title: Africa CDC Youth Public Health & Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 for Young African Professionals
summary: Young African professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, and healthcare innovation are invited to join the Africa CDC Youth Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 , a three-day virtual hands-on training taking place from 27–29 July 2026 . The training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa to strengthen their practical skills in research design, research methodology, and concept note development . Key Details Program: Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 Dates: 27–29 July 2026 Duration: 3 days Format: Virtual Participants: 100 young professionals from across Africa Eligibility: Exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Focus Areas: Research design, research methodology, and concept note development Collaboration: West African Institute of Public Health Network: Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN), an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program Join YiDHN: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn About the Africa CDC Youth Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 The Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop 2026 is designed to equip young African professionals with practical skills to strengthen their capacity to conduct research and contribute to innovation in public and digital health. Taking place virtually from 27 to 29 July 2026 , the three-day hands-on workshop will provide participants with practical knowledge in research design, research methodology, and the development of strong concept notes. Organized in collaboration with the West African Institute of Public Health , the training will bring together 100 young professionals from across Africa , creating an opportunity to build research capacity, foster collaboration, and advance digital health innovation across the continent. What Will Participants Learn? The training will focus on three core areas: Research Design: Strengthening participants ability to develop structured and relevant research approaches. Research Methodology: Building practical knowledge of methods and approaches for conducting effective research. Concept Note Development: Developing the skills needed to prepare clear and compelling research concept notes. Participants will also have the opportunity to connect with other young professionals interested in public health, digital health, research, technology, and healthcare innovation across Africa. Who Can Participate? The Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop is exclusively for members of the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) . The workshop will accommodate 100 young professionals from across Africa who are interested in strengthening their research capacity and contributing to digital health innovation. Those who are not yet members of YiDHN can join the network through the onboarding form. About the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) The Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) is an initiative under the Africa CDC Youth Program aimed at empowering young professionals across Africa to lead the transformation of healthcare through digital solutions. The network brings together young people passionate about digital health and provides opportunities to connect, build capacity, collaborate, and contribute to shaping the future of healthcare in Africa. Through the network, young professionals can also gain access to future training, mentorship, networking, and capacity-building opportunities . Why Join the YiDHN? Africa s rapidly evolving digital health landscape creates significant opportunities for young professionals to contribute to healthcare transformation through research, technology, innovation, and collaboration. By joining YiDHN, young professionals can become part of a growing continental network focused on fostering innovation, building capacity, and driving impactful change in digital health across Africa . Membership also provides an avenue to learn about opportunities such as the Public Health Digital Health Research Training Workshop and future initiatives for young digital health professionals. How to Join the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network Interested young professionals can complete the Africa Youths in Digital Health Network (YiDHN) Onboarding Form to join the network. Join the YiDHN here: https://bit.ly/join_yidhn Join a community of young African professionals working to advance digital health innovation, research, capacity building, and healthcare transformation across Africa . title: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Fellowship 2026 in Geneva, Switzerland | CHF 6,000 Monthly Stipend | Open Worldwide
summary: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is offering a Fellowship opportunity with the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) in Geneva, Switzerland. The fellowship has a contract duration of 12 months, with the possibility to renew, and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 6,000. Key Details Organization: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Eligibility: Open to applicants worldwide who meet the requirements. Fellowship: Fellowship 26229-FEL Section: WIPO Knowledge Center, IP Futures and Knowledge Management Section, Administration, Finance and Management Sector Duty Station: CH-Geneva Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland Contract Duration: 12 months Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026 Publication Date: 22-Jul-2026 Application Deadline: 06-Aug-2026, 10:59:00 PM Grade: N/A IMPORTANT NOTICE REGARDING APPLICATION DEADLINE: Please note that the deadline for applications is indicated in local time as per the time zone of the applicant s location. 1. Organizational context (a) Organizational Setting The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is a United Nations specialized agency. Its WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC) is the custodian of the knowledge repository, which is an authoritative source for global IP academic research. The WKC oversees WIPO’s physical and digital library collection, in addition to the dissemination of WIPO publications. The WKC team requires a qualified Fellow to support the library and knowledge services by collecting, analyzing, and reporting data that informs evidence-based decision-making. Working closely with colleagues, the fellow will contribute to the assessment of library services, digital resources, and user engagement, helping to identify opportunities to improve discoverability, accessibility, and service delivery. Fellowships aim to provide fellows with experience to strengthen their knowledge and professional competence, which they can apply in their professional field once they have completed their fellowship with WIPO. (b) Reporting Lines The Fellow shall work under the supervision of the Head of the WIPO Knowledge Center (WKC). (c) Objectives During the fellowship, the Fellow will assist with the WKC activities and gain in-depth knowledge and competence in the respective field. 2. Duties and responsibilities The Fellow will provide support in the following areas: a) Collect, validate, and manage quantitative and qualitative data relating to library services, digital collections, and information resources. b) Gather, monitor, and analyze usage statistics from library platforms, repositories, websites, and other digital services. c) Produce regular statistical reports to support strategic planning and operational decision-making. d) Analyze trends in resource usage, identifying patterns and opportunities for improvement. e) Assist in developing and maintaining key performance indicators (KPIs) for library services and digital initiatives. f) Contribute to the evaluation of digital resources, collections, and services using evidence-based assessment techniques. g) Assist in collecting and analyzing citation, bibliometric, altmetric, and other research impact data, where applicable. f) Prepare reports, presentations, and briefing materials summarizing analytical findings for internal stakeholders. h) Collaborate with colleagues to improve workflows for data collection, reporting, and assessment. i) Perform other related duties as required. 3. Requirements (a) Education Essential: At least a first-level degree in library, information science, knowledge management or a related field. Recognized professional qualification. (b) Experience Essential: At least two years of professional experience working in a library, knowledge management, research support, or related environment. Experience collecting, managing, and analyzing library or information-related data. Experience working with usage statistics, service metrics, or other performance data to support assessment activities. Experience preparing analytical reports and presenting findings to support decision-making. Experience using spreadsheet software and data analysis tools. Desirable: Experience working with integrated library systems, institutional repositories, discovery platforms, or digital library services. Experience using business intelligence, dashboard, or data visualization tools. Experience working with bibliometric, altmetric, or research impact indicators. Experience with SQL, Python, R, or other analytical tools would be an advantage. (c) Languages Essential: Excellent (written and spoken) knowledge of English. Desirable: Good knowledge of at least one of WIPO s other official languages would be an advantage. (d) Specific skills and competencies Essential: Sound understanding of library operations and digital information services. Knowledge of library assessment methodologies and performance measurement. Ability to collect, clean, organize, and interpret data from multiple sources. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail. Ability to identify trends and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Good understanding of statistical concepts and data visualization principles. Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team. Excellent written and oral communication skills. 4. Organizational competencies Communicating effectively. Showing team spirit. Demonstrating integrity. Valuing diversity. Producing results. Showing service orientation. Seeing the big picture. Seeking change and innovation. Developing yourself and others. 5. Terms and conditions a) Term of fellowship: A fellowship may be granted for a period of up to 12 months with the possibility to renew. b) Anticipated Start Date: October 1, 2026. c) Location: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland. d) Stipend: CHF 6,000 monthly. e) Travel expenses: WIPO shall contribute towards the cost of the fellow’s travel on engagement and separation from service. If necessary, WIPO may provide assistance in obtaining an entry visa to Switzerland. f) WIPO contributes towards the medical insurance and provides accident insurance coverage during the course of the fellowship. g) WIPO will request a “carte de legitimation” for the Fellow, which serves as a residence and work permit, from the Permanent Mission of Switzerland to the United Nations Office and to the other international organizations in Geneva. Family members of the Fellow are not eligible for a “carte de legitimation.” h) Tax and social security: Fellows shall be solely responsible for meeting any taxation and social security obligations that may arise directly or indirectly from their contract with WIPO. FOR MORE INFO AND TO APPLY NOW CLICK HERE Additional information WIPO values diversity among its personnel and is committed to equal employment opportunities. We welcome applications from qualified candidates from unrepresented Member States of WIPO, and from underrepresented geographical regions and groups, including people with disabilities. If candidates need any accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, they should contact their HR focal point when they receive an invitation. Fellows are not staff members of WIPO, and the position does not lead to any employment rights and entitlements beyond the terms of the fellowship. The Fellowship will take place in Geneva, Switzerland and it cannot be carried out remotely. By completing an application, candidates understand that any willful misrepresentation made on this web site, or on any other documents submitted to WIPO during the application, may result in disqualification from the recruitment process, or termination of employment with WIPO at a later date, if that employment resulted from such willful misrepresentations. In the event that your candidature is shortlisted, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of an identification and of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. WIPO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU) / United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/ . Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and these will be reviewed individually. Additional testing/interviewing may be used as a form of screening. Initial appointment is subject to satisfactory professional references. title: Call for Applications: The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program (2026-2027)
summary: OVERVIEW In 2023, the CVF-V20 and the Boston University Global Development Policy Center launched the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program for finance officials (or equivalent) from CVF-V20 Member Countries. The Fellowship Program is an integral part of the CVF-V20’s ongoing efforts to promote and drive ambitious climate action and to mobilize international support for climate vulnerable nations. The aim of the V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is to engender cooperation among CVF-V20 member states, provide them with the tools to combat challenges they may face in the pursuit of strategies to avert climate breakdown, and pioneer the development of economic and financial solutions, including the mobilization of domestic climate finance towards positive climate action. The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program is designed to provide mid- to senior career officials with opportunities for peer-learning, building cutting-edge technical skills to integrate climate change into their work, and supporting their leadership in advancing innovative solutions. The CVF-V20 has consistently emphasized the need to reform the international financial architecture to unlock opportunities on the ground to promote climate prosperity. Through weekly webinars, interactions with experts, residencies, and immersive exercises, V20 Climate Prosperity Fellows will have a unique opportunity to work together in advancing a fit for purpose international financial architecture. COLLABORATION OBJECTIVES At the end of the program, Fellows are expected to be well positioned to support resource mobilization for Climate Prosperity Plans and to: Understand the international financial architecture and be able to identify opportunities to support climate prosperity; Engage in policy discussions concerning reform of the international financial architecture; Harness the knowledge and skills needed to engage and access processes associated with the international financial architecture, including on debt reform, shifting of financial flows, carbon financing exchanges, and mainstream surveillance of climate risks to drive new investment; Identify and deploy communications strategies used to raise awareness of the priorities of the climate-vulnerable countries in relation to the reform of the international financial architecture; and Contribute to the formulation and implementation of their countries’ Climate Prosperity Plans. TARGET OUTCOME To provide peer-learning and technical enhancement support to the finance ministries (or equivalent) of 16 to 20 CVF-V20 member countries by equipping Fellows with skills to pursue the mobilization of financial resources more effectively to support ambitious national climate prosperity plans for development positive climate action. KEY ACTIVITIES Participation in online classes/seminars/workshops; Participation in one-week in-person residencies in January 2027 and October 2027; Participation in relevant meetings, supported by the CVF-V20; Participation in interactive discussions with representatives of International Financial Institutions and partner groups with the support of the CVF-V20; and Preparation and delivery of presentations during V20 Senior Officials Meetings and relevant CVF-V20 workshops and events. CONDITIONS OF PARTICIPATION Candidates from Ministries of Finance (or equivalent) in CVF-V20 member countries who meet the requirements set out below are invited to apply to participate in the year-long Fellowship Program for the period 2026- 2027: Citizen of a CVF-V20 member country; Official with demonstrated five to ten years of mid- to senior-level experience in international affairs, public policy and/or development, including climate/environmental/sustainable development; Committed to participate in the Fellowship program’s activities organized throughout the year, both online and in-person and to complete and submit assignments as required; Willingness to travel abroad to attend in person meetings and training sessions with members of their cohort; Commitment to attend scheduled weekly virtual sessions for the duration of the fellowship period; Committed to working and sharing information with their national government and national stakeholders after the completion of the Fellowship; Committed to integrating into the growing network of V20 CPP fellows and staying engaged in the community to advance common priorities and mutual learning; and Proﬁcient in English. *Prospective Fellows interested in undertaking intensive training in debt sustainability analyses should indicate the same in their application and, in so doing, commit to an additional session to undertake this training each week. Proficiency in using Microsoft Excel and familiarity with macroeconomic concepts are recommended. APPLICATION PROCESS Interested officials must submit their application by accomplishing the form: Submit your application here The deadline for submission of applications is on 31 July 2026. TENTATIVE FELLOWSHIP TIMELINE Month August 2026 Selection and notification of Fellows September 2026 Finance Ministries (or equivalent) provide official confirmation of selected Fellows’ participation in the Program October 2026 Weekly webinars begin and continue throughout the year January 2027 First in-person residency *Location will be confirmed in due course January 2027 Proposals for capstone projects submitted for feedback March 2027 Fellows provide inputs to the V20 Senior Officials Meeting March 2027 Virtual Meeting Fellows contribute to preparations for the Spring Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, including through the identification of priorities, policy goals, and strategies with the goal to put together a singular document for Spring Meetings priorities, with the possibility of sharing externally, as well as to the V20 Communiqué. April 2027 2027 Spring Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group Fellows contribute to the hybrid sessions on topics relevant to the CVF-V20 Virtual or in-person participation during the 18th V20 Ministerial Dialogue October 2027 Second in-person residency *Location will be confirmed in due course Presentation of final capstone projects Conclusion of the program and graduation KEY CONTACTS For additional information about the program and application process, please contact: Christian F. Soqueño Deputy Director for Fellowships, Membership and Partnerships Coordination +63 9175932773 christian.soqueno@cvfv20.org Farrah Brown Diplomacy Lead, Membership and Partnerships Coordination +1 9175269281 farrah.brown@cvfv20.org CVF-V20 Secretariat secretariat@cvfv20.org Source: https://cvfv20.org/call-for-applications-the-v20-climate-prosperity-fellowship-program-2026-2027/ The post Call for Applications: The V20 Climate Prosperity Fellowship Program (2026-2027) appeared first on Opportunities for Youth .

title: UNDP Call for Proposals 2026: Funding Opportunity for CSOs and NGOs to End Violence Against Women and Girls in Africa
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Ethiopia has announced a Call for Proposals for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and NGOs under the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . This opportunity invites eligible civil society organizations to submit proposals to contribute to efforts aimed at ending violence against women and girls across Africa. The initiative provides an opportunity for organizations working on gender equality, women s rights, prevention of gender-based violence, advocacy, community engagement, and related areas to participate in a major regional programme. Applications must be submitted through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal by 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM New York time . About the UNDP Call for Proposals The call is managed by UNDP Ethiopia and relates to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . The programme seeks to support efforts to address violence against women and girls through collaboration with civil society organizations and other partners. Opportunity at a Glance Organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office: UNDP Ethiopia Programme: Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 Focus: Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) Contract Type: Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Duty Station: Home-based Programme Duration: August 2026 – December 2028 Expected Start Date: Upon signing of the agreement Application Deadline: 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM New York time Reference Number: UNDP-ETH-00754 Contact: info.procurementet@undp.org Who Can Apply? The call is specifically targeted at Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) . Organizations interested in applying should carefully review the official solicitation and negotiation documents available through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal to determine the full eligibility, technical, administrative, and documentation requirements. Applicants should ensure that the organization name entered during supplier registration is the full legal name corresponding with the organization s legal and bank account records . About the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme 2.0 The services under this call relate to the Spotlight Initiative Africa Regional Programme (SIARP) 2.0 to End Violence Against Women and Girls (EVAWG) . The programme focuses on efforts to address violence against women and girls in Africa and strengthen action toward gender equality and women s rights. Civil society organizations have an important role in this work, including through community engagement, advocacy, prevention, service delivery, accountability, and advancing the rights and agency of women and girls. Applicants should consult the official tender documents for the precise scope of work, expected results, deliverables, eligibility criteria, and proposal requirements. Contract Duration and Location The assignment is expected to run from August 2026 through December 2028 , with the agreement commencing upon signing. The duty station is listed as home-based , making this a particularly relevant opportunity for qualifying organizations capable of contributing to the programme s regional objectives without being based at a UNDP office. How to Apply for the UNDP CSO Call for Proposals Applications must be submitted electronically through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal . Interested organizations should: Register on the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal if they do not already have a supplier profile. If already registered, log in using the existing supplier account. Do not create another profile. Search for the negotiation using reference number UNDP-ETH-00754 . Subscribe to the tender to receive notifications about amendments or updates. Create a draft response in the system to indicate your intention to submit a proposal. This enables UNDP to send relevant notifications if the tender requirements are amended. Review all negotiation and solicitation documents carefully before preparing the application. Submit the complete offer directly through the Quantum Supplier Portal before the deadline. Organizations that have previously registered but cannot remember their login details should use the forgotten password/username functionality rather than creating a new account. Questions or requests for clarification should be submitted using the messaging functionality available within the procurement system, in accordance with the solicitation instructions. Important Information for Applicants When registering in the supplier portal, applicants should enter the organization s full legal name exactly as it appears in its legal and bank account documentation . Organizations should also subscribe to the tender after locating it in Quantum. This is important because UNDP may issue amendments, clarifications, or updates before the submission deadline. Interested CSOs are strongly encouraged to begin the registration and application process early to allow sufficient time to review the solicitation documents and resolve any supplier portal issues. Application Deadline The deadline for submissions is: 29 July 2026 at 4:00 AM (New York time). Applications must be submitted directly through the UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal in accordance with the requirements of the solicitation. Given the deadline, prospective applicants should review the opportunity and begin preparing their submissions as soon as possible. Official Application and Further Information Tender Reference: UNDP-ETH-00754 Application Portal: UNDP Quantum Supplier Portal UNDP Resources for Bidders: Applicants can consult UNDP s procurement resources for guidance on supplier registration, using the Quantum system, and submitting bids. Procurement Office: UNDP Ethiopia Procurement Unit Contact Email: info.procurementet@undp.org Applicants should rely on the official UNDP procurement notice and solicitation documents for the definitive eligibility criteria, requirements, deadlines, and application instructions. title: Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026: Fully Funded Remote Fellowship Offering $3,000 Stipend for Emerging Economic Policy Leaders
summary: The Roosevelt Institute is inviting experienced policy professionals, researchers, academics, and experts to apply for the Good Life Residents Program 2026 , a prestigious six-month remote residency designed to cultivate innovative policy leaders and generate transformative ideas that advance economic justice in the United States. As part of the Roosevelt Institute s broader Good Life Agenda , selected residents will work alongside leading economists, policy experts, researchers, and senior advisors to develop original policy proposals addressing some of the country s most pressing economic challenges. Participants will produce policy essays, collaborate with subject matter experts, contribute to national policy conversations, and receive $3,000 in compensation , along with travel and accommodation support for the program s concluding event if required. One of the featured residency tracks is the AI and Finance Residents Program , created in partnership with Data Society , which focuses on examining how artificial intelligence is transforming finance, investment, labor markets, industrial policy, and the broader economy. This residency provides an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who are passionate about shaping public policy, promoting equitable economic growth, and influencing the future of AI governance. About the Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month policy residency that brings together a small cohort of emerging and established policy thinkers to explore solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute s vision for a stronger and more equitable economy. Rather than conducting traditional academic research, residents focus on producing practical, people-centered policy ideas that can influence public debate and policymaking. The program emphasizes collaboration, mentorship, public engagement, and intellectual exchange. Throughout the residency, participants work closely with: Roosevelt Institute Think Tank directors Senior organizational leadership Topic advisors Fellow residents Policy practitioners Academic experts Organizers and government leaders Each residency concludes with a public event designed to amplify participants ideas and encourage dialogue on important national and state-level policy issues. AI and Finance Residents Program One of the Roosevelt Institute s featured residency topics explores the rapidly evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and finance. Massive investments in generative AI have significantly reshaped the economy, influencing: Stock markets Financial markets Corporate profits Bond issuance Employment trends Industrial development Trade policy Technology investment Economic growth Today, just seven technology companies account for more than one-third of the total market capitalization of the S P 500, raising concerns about market concentration, financial stability, and economic inequality. The Roosevelt Institute, together with Data Society , seeks residents capable of producing bold policy ideas that help redirect AI investment toward broader public benefit while protecting workers, strengthening democratic institutions, and encouraging sustainable innovation. Objectives of the AI and Finance Residency The residency seeks to answer important policy questions such as: How can governments better oversee private AI investments? How can policymakers reduce excessive concentration within the technology sector? How can AI investment benefit society rather than only large corporations? How can governments encourage investment across other important sectors of the economy? How should AI policy balance innovation, public safety, labor protections, and national competitiveness? What democratic institutions are needed to ensure accountability over public investments in AI? How can governments support technology research that strengthens supply chains and sustainability? Participants are encouraged to propose original, practical, and people-centered policy recommendations. What Residents Will Do Successful applicants will participate in numerous activities throughout the six-month residency. These include: Develop Original Policy Essays Residents will research and write an approximately 1,500-word policy essay presenting innovative solutions aligned with the Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Agenda. Each essay responds to a specific policy prompt within the resident s assigned topic area. Join a Small Collaborative Cohort Each topic area consists of only three to four residents , creating an environment that encourages meaningful collaboration, peer learning, and intellectual exchange. Residents will work closely with one another throughout the program. Work with Expert Advisors Every cohort is supported by one or two Topic Advisors. These advisors include: Leading academics Government practitioners Policy leaders Organizers Industry experts They provide: Intellectual mentorship Strategic guidance Feedback on policy proposals Moderation during discussions and public events Participate in Public Events At the end of the residency, participants present and discuss their policy ideas during a public event organized by the Roosevelt Institute. The event helps amplify participants work while encouraging national dialogue around economic policy. Contribute to Public Engagement Residents may also participate in: Opinion editorials (Op-Eds) Press interviews Reporter briefings Public policy discussions Media engagement opportunities Serve as Good Life Agenda Ambassadors Participants are expected to promote and represent the Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Agenda throughout their professional and public networks. Program Structure Each residency topic includes: 3–4 Good Life Residents 1–2 senior Topic Advisors Roosevelt Institute policy staff Organizational leadership support The program emphasizes mentorship, collaboration, and practical policy development. Program Duration The residency lasts: Six months Time Commitment Residents should expect to dedicate approximately: 5–8 hours per month This makes the residency suitable for professionals balancing existing work or academic responsibilities. Location The program is primarily: Remote However, participants may be invited to travel for selected meetings or the final public event. Compensation Selected residents will receive: $3,000 stipend Travel expenses covered (if required) Accommodation for the concluding event (if required) This financial support enables participants to fully engage in the residency while contributing meaningful policy work. Who Should Apply? The Roosevelt Institute encourages applications from individuals with substantial experience in policy development, technology, economics, or related fields. Ideal applicants include: Policy professionals Researchers Economists Academics Government practitioners Technology policy experts AI researchers Industrial policy specialists Think tank professionals Candidates should demonstrate both subject expertise and a commitment to developing policies that improve economic outcomes for society. Required Qualifications Successful applicants should have: Demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence, technology policy, industrial policy, or a related discipline. A minimum of five years of professional or academic policy experience . Strong analytical and writing abilities. An interest in advancing equitable economic policy. The ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary teams. A commitment to contributing original policy ideas. Benefits of Joining the Program Participants will enjoy numerous professional benefits, including: $3,000 financial compensation. National exposure through public events. Collaboration with leading policy experts. Individual mentorship from senior advisors. Opportunity to publish original policy work. Professional networking opportunities. Media and press engagement. Flexible remote participation. Travel and accommodation support for program events. Contribution to shaping future AI and economic policy discussions. Why This Residency Matters Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming economies worldwide. While AI offers tremendous opportunities for innovation and productivity, it also presents challenges related to wealth concentration, labor markets, financial stability, public accountability, and democratic governance. The Roosevelt Institute s Good Life Residents Program seeks individuals capable of proposing practical policy solutions that ensure AI serves broader public interests rather than reinforcing existing inequalities. Participants have the opportunity to contribute directly to one of today s most important public policy conversations while helping shape future economic policy. How to Apply Interested applicants should visit the Roosevelt Institute s official Good Life Residents Program webpage and complete the online application according to the published application instructions. Applicants should carefully review all eligibility requirements before submitting their materials. APPLY NOW Application Deadline Please read and complete this application by the end of the day on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to be considered for the Good Life Residents Program on AI, presented by the Roosevelt Institute and Data Society. Reach out to rooseveltsociety@rooseveltinstitute.org with any questions or concerns. Program Term: 6 months (September–February 2027) Time Commitment: Part-Time (~5–8 hours/month) Location: Remote; Travel may be requested for select convenings Conclusion The Roosevelt Institute Good Life Residents Program 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced policy professionals and researchers to shape conversations around artificial intelligence, finance, and economic justice. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, public engagement, and a funded six-month residency, participants can develop innovative policy ideas capable of influencing national discussions and future policymaking. For individuals passionate about AI governance, economic equity, and public policy, this residency provides a unique platform to contribute meaningful solutions while expanding professional networks and gaining national visibility. title: AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026: Apply for the Free Aspen Policy Academy Program to Develop Civic AI Policy Solutions in the United States
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming societies, economies, governments, and public services. As governments increasingly integrate AI into policymaking and service delivery, there is a growing need for innovative civic leaders who can develop responsible, equitable, and community-centered AI policy solutions. To help address this challenge, the Aspen Policy Academy has launched applications for the AI Civic Action Accelerator 2026 , a free virtual accelerator program designed for individuals and small teams seeking to develop impactful AI policy initiatives that strengthen the relationship between governments, communities, and artificial intelligence. This unique accelerator combines policy education, expert mentorship, peer collaboration, and practical project development to help participants transform promising ideas into actionable policy solutions capable of creating real public impact. If you are passionate about civic technology, responsible AI governance, public policy, or community innovation, this program offers an exceptional opportunity to refine your ideas and present them directly to policymakers. About the AI Civic Action Accelerator The AI Civic Action Accelerator is a free six-session virtual accelerator created by Aspen Policy Academy. The accelerator is specifically designed for early-stage civic AI policy projects that seek to improve how governments, communities, and artificial intelligence interact. Rather than focusing on building AI products, the program emphasizes developing policy solutions that help governments respond to emerging AI challenges while ensuring AI serves the public interest. Participants receive structured guidance to refine their ideas, strengthen their policy proposals, and develop practical advocacy strategies capable of influencing local or state-level decision-making. The accelerator is ideal for applicants who already have a promising idea but need support turning it into an effective, evidence-based policy initiative. Program Objectives The AI Civic Action Accelerator aims to help participants: Develop practical civic AI policy solutions. Learn a proven framework for influencing public policy. Receive personalized feedback from experienced instructors. Collaborate with peers working on similar civic challenges. Build an implementation strategy for policy change. Produce tangible policy outputs. Present solutions directly to policymakers. Rather than simply teaching policy theory, the accelerator focuses on helping participants produce work that can be implemented in real communities. Areas of Interest The Aspen Policy Academy is looking for innovative policy ideas addressing civic AI challenges such as: Improving Civic Participation Projects may explore ways AI can: Improve public consultation Increase citizen engagement Enhance democratic participation Make government communication more accessible Youth Online Safety Applicants may propose policy solutions that: Protect young people online Improve digital literacy Address AI-generated misinformation Promote safer online environments Transparent Government AI Potential ideas include: Responsible AI use within government Transparent decision-making Ethical AI governance Accountability frameworks Fair AI implementation Workforce and Employment Applicants may also propose solutions that address: AI automation Workforce transitions Job displacement Government workforce policies Future-of-work planning Other Civic AI Challenges The accelerator welcomes creative policy ideas that strengthen relationships between: Governments Communities Artificial intelligence What Participants Will Learn Throughout the six-session accelerator, participants will learn Aspen Policy Academy s proven framework for creating policy impact. Key learning areas include: 1. Problem Scoping Participants learn how to: Clearly define policy problems Identify underlying causes Narrow broad issues into actionable challenges 2. Stakeholder Analysis Participants identify: Government agencies Community organizations Decision-makers Partners Opponents Beneficiaries 3. Policy Alternatives Participants evaluate: Existing policy approaches Alternative interventions Policy feasibility Practical implementation options 4. Developing Policy Outputs Participants create practical deliverables that may include: Policy briefs Strategy documents Advocacy materials Community engagement plans Implementation roadmaps 5. Advocacy Planning The program teaches participants how to: Engage policymakers Build public support Present evidence effectively Develop advocacy campaigns 6. Policy Pitching The accelerator concludes with participants presenting their refined policy solutions directly to a real decision-maker. Program Structure The accelerator consists of: Six live virtual sessions Two hours per session Interactive instruction Hands-on workshops Peer collaboration Individual project development Assignments between sessions Guided readings Each session combines classroom learning with practical workshopping. title: Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action: Free Global Online Course by UNITAR and C40 with UN Digital Certificate
summary: Climate change is one of the greatest challenges facing humanity today, and women are increasingly recognized as powerful drivers of innovative, inclusive, and sustainable climate solutions. To strengthen women s capacity to lead meaningful environmental change, the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR), in partnership with C40 Cities and with the exclusive support of the Fondation L Oréal, has launched the Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action online course. This self-paced international e-learning programme is designed to inspire, educate, and empower women and girls to become effective climate leaders capable of developing and implementing inclusive climate initiatives within their communities and beyond. Whether you are just beginning your climate leadership journey or already working on environmental projects, this comprehensive online course provides the scientific knowledge, leadership skills, and practical tools needed to transform climate ideas into impactful actions. About the Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action Course The Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action course is an international online learning programme that equips women and girls with the knowledge and confidence needed to tackle climate challenges through inclusive leadership. The programme combines climate science with practical leadership development, enabling learners to understand climate issues while learning how to design, lead, and advocate for equitable climate solutions. Developed through a collaboration between globally respected organizations, the course brings together expertise from: United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) C40 Cities Fondation L Oréal Columbia Climate School CARE France The programme recognizes that although women are among those most affected by climate change, they remain significantly underrepresented in climate decision-making processes. By strengthening leadership capacity, the course seeks to bridge this gap and encourage greater participation of women in climate governance and action. Why This Course Matters Climate change affects every country, yet its impacts are not distributed equally. Women and girls often experience disproportionate effects due to existing social and economic inequalities. At the same time, women play an essential role in developing resilient communities, promoting sustainable practices, and advancing climate justice. This course addresses these realities by helping participants: Understand climate science. Learn the principles of inclusive climate action. Build confidence as climate leaders. Develop practical climate projects. Influence decision-makers and communities. Promote equitable climate solutions. Create resilient and sustainable communities. The course emphasizes that climate action must be both environmentally effective and socially inclusive. What You Will Learn By completing this programme, participants will gain a broad understanding of climate change alongside practical leadership skills. Upon completion, learners will be able to: 1. Understand Climate Change Participants will learn: What climate change is The causes of global warming The impacts of climate change worldwide Scientific foundations of climate science Climate mitigation and adaptation strategies 2. Understand Inclusive Climate Action Learners will explore: Climate justice Equity in climate policies Inclusive environmental decision-making Community participation Sustainable development approaches 3. Explore Women s Role in Climate Action Participants will examine: Why women are central to climate solutions Gender inequalities within climate governance Women s contributions to environmental sustainability Leadership opportunities for women in climate action 4. Plan Effective Climate Projects The course introduces practical methods for: Identifying community climate challenges Designing impactful projects Developing implementation strategies Managing climate initiatives Evaluating project outcomes 5. Strengthen Leadership Skills Participants will develop skills in: Leadership Communication Advocacy Collaboration Decision-making Strategic planning Team building 6. Influence Others and Build Support Learners will understand how to: Advocate for climate action Engage stakeholders Mobilize communities Communicate climate solutions effectively Inspire collective action 7. Build Personal Resilience Climate leadership often involves overcoming challenges. Participants will also learn techniques for: Maintaining motivation Building resilience Managing obstacles Sustaining long-term climate engagement Course Structure The course contains five comprehensive sections that guide learners from climate science fundamentals to practical project development. Module 1: Introduction to Climate Change and Inclusive Climate Action This introductory module covers: Climate science fundamentals Causes of climate change Environmental impacts Social implications Principles of inclusive climate action Module 2: Women at the Heart of Climate Action This module focuses on: Women s leadership Gender equality Climate justice Women s role in sustainable development Real-world examples of women-led climate initiatives Module 3: Taking the Lead on Inclusive Climate Action Participants learn practical leadership approaches including: Project planning Community engagement Inclusive leadership techniques Climate project development Module 4: Influencing Change While Staying Resilient Topics include: Communication strategies Advocacy Stakeholder engagement Leadership resilience Building long-term impact Module 5: Course Wrap-Up The final section provides: Practical guidance Climate project development tools Action planning resources Recommendations for future climate leadership Course Duration The programme requires approximately: 9 hours of learning 3 practical exercises Entirely self-paced learning Participants can complete the course according to their own schedule without fixed class times. Languages Available To ensure global accessibility, the course is offered in: English French Spanish This multilingual approach enables participants from different regions of the world to benefit from the training. Certification Participants who successfully complete the course can obtain an official UNITAR Digital Certificate . To qualify: Score at least 70% on all quizzes. Learners have three attempts per quiz. After passing all quizzes, participants may purchase the official digital certificate for USD 30 . The digital certificate allows graduates to: Verify their achievement online. Share their accomplishment with employers. Strengthen professional profiles. Demonstrate climate leadership skills. Interested applicants should click HERE Learn more about the course HERE Benefit of Taking This Course Participants will gain numerous professional and personal benefits, including: International training from a United Nations institution. Self-paced online learning. Flexible study schedule. Comprehensive climate science education. Leadership development. Practical project planning skills. Knowledge of inclusive climate action. Global perspectives from leading climate experts. Opportunity to earn a recognized UN digital certificate. Enhanced career prospects in sustainability and climate-related fields. Improved advocacy and communication skills. Access to practical tools for launching climate initiatives. Organizations Behind the Programme UNITAR The United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) develops innovative learning solutions that strengthen global decision-making and sustainable development. UNITAR supports governments, organizations, and individuals worldwide, with particular attention to developing countries, Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and vulnerable communities. C40 Cities C40 Cities is a global network of nearly 100 major cities committed to tackling climate change. The organization works with city leaders, businesses, civil society, youth movements, and experts to: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Promote climate resilience. Advance equitable climate policies. Support sustainable urban development. Fondation L Oréal The Fondation L Oréal supports women through initiatives focused on: Scientific research Climate action Women s empowerment Inclusive development Its Women and Climate programme specifically supports women leading innovative climate projects and promotes gender-sensitive climate solutions worldwide. Why You Should Enroll If you want to become part of the global movement addressing climate change, this course provides an excellent foundation. Whether you are: A student, An environmental advocate, A young professional, A community organizer, A policymaker, An entrepreneur, Or simply passionate about protecting the planet, this programme equips you with the knowledge, leadership skills, and confidence needed to create meaningful environmental impact. Because the course is self-paced, learners can complete it alongside their studies or professional commitments, making it accessible regardless of their schedule. Conclusion The Developing Skills for Women Leadership in Climate Action course is more than an online training programme—it is an opportunity to empower women and girls to become leaders in one of the world s most pressing challenges. By combining climate science, leadership development, and practical project planning, the programme prepares participants to create inclusive and equitable climate solutions within their communities and beyond. Delivered by UNITAR in partnership with C40 Cities and supported by Fondation L Oréal, the course reflects international expertise and a commitment to advancing women s leadership in climate action. With flexible self-paced learning, multilingual content, and the opportunity to earn a recognized UN digital certificate, this programme is an outstanding opportunity for aspiring climate leaders across the globe to build the skills necessary to drive meaningful and lasting environmental change. title: Climate Action Reserve Remote Jobs 2026: Apply for Analyst, Associate and Senior Associate Program Operations Positions in the United States
summary: Are you interested in climate change, carbon markets, carbon credits, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, environmental sustainability, or climate action? The Climate Action Reserve is offering exciting full-time remote career opportunities for qualified candidates to join its Program Operations team as an Analyst, Associate, or Senior Associate . These positions provide an opportunity to contribute to one of the leading carbon crediting programs while supporting projects designed to quantify and verify greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals. Successful candidates will work in a professional, mission-driven environment focused on advancing credible, transparent, and market-based solutions to climate change. The available roles are remote and based in the United States. However, applicants must maintain legal authorization to work in the United States for the entire duration of their employment. The organization does not sponsor work visas or cover relocation expenses. About the Climate Action Reserve The Climate Action Reserve is a nonprofit organization established under Section 501(c)(3) of the United States tax code. Its vision is to create a world in which people and institutions cooperate to address climate change at speed and scale. The organization’s mission is to develop and implement trusted market-based programs that advance climate action for both people and the planet. A significant part of the Climate Action Reserve’s work involves carbon crediting. Through its programs, the organization develops high-quality standards for measuring and quantifying greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals. It also registers projects that meet the required standards, issues carbon credits associated with verified climate benefits, and maintains a transparent and publicly accessible registry system. This makes the organization an important participant in the broader carbon market and climate action ecosystem. Job Opportunity: Program Operations Analyst, Associate and Senior Associate The Climate Action Reserve is seeking candidates to join its Program Operations team. Depending on the applicant’s experience, qualifications, and level of expertise, candidates may be considered for one of three levels: Analyst Associate Senior Associate The exact duties, level of independence, and responsibilities will vary depending on the seniority of the successful candidate. The Program Operations team supports both the substantive and administrative functions of the organization’s carbon crediting programs. Employees in the team help ensure that carbon projects are properly reviewed, administered, monitored, and operated in accordance with established protocols and program requirements. Key Responsibilities Successful candidates may be responsible for a range of technical, administrative, analytical, and operational duties. 1. Review Carbon Project Documentation One of the key responsibilities of Program Operations staff is to review documentation submitted by carbon projects. This may include: Reviewing carbon project submissions. Examining verification documentation. Assessing project-related materials against applicable program requirements. Identifying inconsistencies, missing information, or areas requiring clarification. Supporting the evaluation of documentation related to emission reductions and removals. This responsibility requires a strong eye for detail and the ability to carefully analyze complex information. Candidates must be comfortable working with confidential materials and handling documents that may contain sensitive project, organizational, or account information. 2. Support Carbon Program Administration and Operations Program Operations staff will also support the day-to-day administration and operation of a growing number of emission reduction and removal projects. This may involve: Supporting the implementation of carbon crediting programs. Helping manage project processes. Coordinating administrative activities. Ensuring that projects move through the appropriate program procedures. Supporting communication and documentation requirements. Helping maintain accurate records and operational information. As the organization continues to manage a growing portfolio of climate projects, the Program Operations team plays an important role in ensuring that processes are efficient, accurate, and consistent. 3. Provide Technical and Administrative Guidance Employees may provide guidance to accountholders and other users of the Climate Action Reserve’s programs and systems. This could include helping users understand: Program procedures. Documentation requirements. Carbon crediting processes. Protocol-related requirements. Administrative procedures. Project submission and verification processes. Strong communication skills are therefore essential. Candidates should be able to explain complex technical or administrative information clearly and professionally to different audiences. 4. Support Protocol Training Program Operations staff may also help deliver and provide training on the organization’s protocols. This could involve: Supporting training sessions. Helping explain carbon crediting protocols. Assisting project developers and verifiers in understanding program requirements. Preparing or supporting training materials. Responding to questions during training activities. This aspect of the role may be particularly suitable for candidates who enjoy knowledge-sharing, professional presentations, technical communication, and working with stakeholders. 5. Participate in Audits and Verification Oversight The role may occasionally involve conducting audits of verification bodies to assess whether they are adhering to programmatic requirements. This responsibility can include: Reviewing verification processes. Assessing compliance with program requirements. Observing verification activities. Supporting audits of verification bodies. Traveling to project locations when required. The position therefore combines remote work with periodic travel. Employees may travel to project sites and events for approximately five to six weeks per year in the United States. Who Can Apply? The Climate Action Reserve is seeking candidates from different professional backgrounds who demonstrate an interest in carbon markets, carbon crediting, carbon accounting, climate action, or related areas. Applicants may demonstrate this interest through: Professional employment. Academic studies. Research. Co-curricular activities. Volunteer experience. Climate-related projects. Environmental or sustainability initiatives. Experience with carbon accounting or emissions-related work. The role is open at different career levels, making it potentially suitable for both entry-level candidates and experienced professionals. Analyst Position The Analyst position is designed for entry-level candidates and does not require prior professional work experience. This may be suitable for applicants who: Have recently completed an undergraduate degree. Are beginning a career in climate action or carbon markets. Have academic or co-curricular experience related to carbon markets or environmental issues. Demonstrate strong analytical and organizational abilities. Have an interest in learning about carbon crediting and greenhouse gas accounting. Associate Position Applicants for the Associate level are generally expected to have at least two years of professional work experience. However, the experience requirement may be reduced for candidates with direct experience in responsibilities relevant to the role. Relevant experience may include work involving: Carbon markets. Carbon crediting. Carbon accounting. Environmental programs. Climate policy. Project operations. Technical documentation review. Compliance. Auditing. Program administration. Stakeholder guidance. Senior Associate Position Applicants for the Senior Associate level are generally expected to have at least five years of professional work experience. The required experience may be reduced for candidates who have particularly relevant experience in the specific responsibilities of the position. Senior-level candidates should be capable of working with a higher level of autonomy and may be expected to take on more complex responsibilities within Program Operations. Essential Qualifications Applicants should meet the following requirements: Professional Experience The required experience depends on the level of the position: Analyst: No prior professional work experience is required. Associate: Generally requires at least two years of professional experience. Senior Associate: Generally requires at least five years of professional experience. Candidates with highly relevant experience in the specific responsibilities of the position may be considered even if they do not meet the standard experience thresholds. Interest in Carbon Markets and Climate Action Applicants must demonstrate an interest in one or more of the following areas: Carbon markets. Carbon crediting. Carbon accounting. Greenhouse gas emissions reduction. Greenhouse gas removals. Climate change mitigation. Environmental sustainability. Climate policy. Market-based climate solutions. This interest may come from professional experience, academic studies, research, extracurricular activities, or other relevant experiences. Strong Attention to Detail The role involves reviewing project documentation, verification materials, and other important information. Applicants should therefore have: Excellent attention to detail. Strong organizational abilities. The ability to identify errors and inconsistencies. The ability to work carefully with confidential materials. A commitment to accuracy. Strong Written Communication Skills Successful candidates must be able to communicate clearly in writing. This may involve: Writing professional emails. Preparing reports. Reviewing documentation. Providing guidance to stakeholders. Documenting project-related information. Communicating technical or administrative requirements. Undergraduate Degree Applicants must have an undergraduate degree. The announcement does not limit applicants to a specific undergraduate major. However, candidates with educational backgrounds related to environmental studies, climate science, sustainability, economics, public policy, political science, business, engineering, accounting, finance, data analysis, or other relevant areas may be able to demonstrate particularly relevant knowledge depending on their experience. Software and Artificial Intelligence Skills Applicants must be proficient in standard workplace software such as: Microsoft Word. Microsoft Excel. Microsoft Outlook. Other standard office and productivity tools. The organization also expects candidates to have proficiency with artificial intelligence tools. Applicants who can demonstrate practical experience using AI tools to improve research, analysis, productivity, document preparation, data organization, or workflow efficiency may be able to strengthen their applications. Professional English Proficiency Applicants must have professional proficiency in English. Strong English communication skills are important because the role involves written communication, technical guidance, stakeholder engagement, documentation review, and training-related activities. Preferred Qualification A graduate or professional degree is preferred. Although this qualification is not listed as essential, candidates with relevant postgraduate education may be considered favorably. Potentially relevant graduate-level backgrounds may include: Environmental management. Climate change. Sustainability. Environmental policy. Public policy. Economics. Business administration.
